stat_test: Friedman test (F1: F_F=11.73, critical F(6,132)=2.07, reject) + Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc, CD=1.94 (k=8, alpha=0.05), Table VIII; SMOTE marked '-' for F1, MCC, ACC. Wilcoxon signed-rank only reported for GOIO vs IDENTITY and GAMO (ACC, p=1) and vs SOS (MCC, p=2.56e-7), Table IX; no Wilcoxon vs SMOTE.

win_claim.quote: Comprehensive experiments on 18 real-world and five synthetic datasets demonstrate that GOIO outperforms the state-of-the-art oversampling methods in F1-score, MCC, and Accuracy.

notes: All results tables are images; pages 9-12 rendered at 200-300 dpi and read visually (Table V cropped at 300 dpi). Cells printed as mean±std(rank); rank kept in marks, std copied as printed (2 decimals). best_other = highest value among IDENTITY, BSMOTE, SMOTETL, MLOS, GAMO, SOS (excluding GOIO and SMOTE); IDENTITY (no resampling) is included in that pool. artificial_0.5_2.5: SOS 0.5344 bold rank 1 and GOIO 0.5344 rank 2 (tie in printed value). Table V has 23 rows = 18 real-world (Table I) + 5 artificial (Table II); dataset name 'taiwanses' copied as printed. Classifier-level breakdown not stated in paper. Other metrics: MCC Table VI (GOIO avg 0.4308, SMOTE 0.3962), Accuracy Table VII. Cross-check with Table I dataset list not done in detail (Table I is an image).
